fact: CIVIX (Cote d'Ivoire Internet Exchange), the national exchange point, has been operational for more than a decade and federates telecom operators and ISPs, per Fraternite Matin reporting the ARTCI PeeringDay 2026 in Abidjan.
Traffic: 36 Gbps (average daily) at CIVIX on 2026-06-15, as stated at the ARTCI PeeringDay 2026; the article gives no measurement date, so the forum date is used.
Netflix and Akamai are among the international content players that CIVIX federates alongside operators and ISPs, per the article on PeeringDay 2026.
CIVIX, the national exchange point created in July 2013, has 14 connected operators and providers, per ARTCI at its first peering forum in Abidjan.
Traffic: 20 Gbps (average, per day) at CIVIX on 2025-08-05, as stated by ARTCI at the first Ivorian peering forum.

ARTCI announced recently the official launch of a third point of presence for CIVIX with Raxio in the neutral data centre at Grand-Bassam, a city other than Abidjan; the article gives no launch date and no members there, so the forum date is used.

Raxio says its Cote d'Ivoire data centre at Grand Bassam hosts carriers, cloud providers and Internet Exchange Points present in the facility; no exchange is named, no member count and no date, so the page date is used.

ARTCI's May 2024 seminar deck says the Netflix cache is hosted at the national exchange point, and that moving the other global content providers' caches there from operators' data centres is under way.
MainOne says customers at its Grand Bassam data centre get access to internet exchanges, including the Amsterdam Internet Exchange (AMS-IX) 'hosted at the data center'.
